n: Since God’s promise of entering His rest still stands, we should be careful that none of us falls short of it.

f.g: Take serious care; be reverently cautious.

n: We have heard the good news just as the Israelites did, but the message didn’t help them because they didn’t combine it with faith. Latter-day scripture likewise teaches the gospel was preached anciently.

f.w: unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them

f.g: United with faith in the hearers.

n: We who believe do enter that rest. God’s works were finished at Creation, so His rest has been available all along — yet unbelievers are shut out.

f.w: As I have sworn in my wrath
from the foundation of the world

n: Scripture says about the seventh day: “God rested on the seventh day from all His works.”

f.w: God did rest the seventh day

n: And in the Psalm again: “They shall not enter My rest.”
So the rest is still open for some to enter, since those who first heard the promise failed to enter because of disobedience.
So God set another day — “Today” — speaking through David centuries later: “Today, if you hear His voice, don’t harden your hearts.”

f.g: In the Psalms, attributed to David.

n: If Joshua had given them the full rest, God wouldn’t have spoken later about another day. “Jesus” here is the Greek form of Joshua, who led Israel into Canaan.

f.g: Joshua — the same name in Greek (Iēsous).

n: So there remains a Sabbath-rest for God’s people.

f.w: a rest to the people of God

n: Whoever enters God’s rest also rests from his own labors, as God did from His.
So let us make every effort to enter that rest, so no one falls by following Israel’s example of disobedience.
God’s word is alive and active, sharper than a double-edged sword. It cuts to our deepest being and judges the thoughts and intentions of our hearts.

f.w: discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart

n: Nothing in creation is hidden from God. Everything is uncovered and exposed before the eyes of the One to whom we must give account.

f.w: him with whom we have to do
f.g: Him to whom we must give an account.

n: Since we have a great High Priest who has passed through the heavens — Jesus, the Son of God — let us hold firmly to the faith we profess.

f.g: As the high priest passed through the veil into the Holy of Holies.

n: Our High Priest isn’t unable to sympathize with our weaknesses. He was tempted in every way as we are, yet He never sinned.

f.w: touched with the feeling of our infirmities

n: So let us come confidently to God’s throne of grace, to receive mercy and find help just when we need it.

f.g: God’s throne pictured as a mercy seat.
